meta.title: Changelog — what shipped in MepMail
meta.description: Every MepMail release, newest first: what changed for you and the day it shipped.

hero.title: What <highlight>shipped</highlight>, release by release.
hero.lead: MepMail is built in the open. This is the list of releases, newest first: what changed for you, dated by the day it shipped.
hero.note: Create a free account: Send starts with no card.

feed.title: Recent releases
feed.body: The {recent, number} most recent releases are open. The {older, number} earlier ones, back to v{first}, are folded right below.

releases.title: Create and open mailboxes over MCP, without trial and error
releases.summary: An agent checks what a mailbox needs before creating it, repeats a create without duplicates and gives itself access to the new mailbox without reconnecting.

items: check_mailbox: before creating (or to diagnose), layer by layer: the requester's role, the domain's verification, whether the address is free, license and seats, receiving and what is left to do, with when it was checked. Seats are never bought over MCP.

grant_mailbox_access and revoke_mailbox_access: an app connected with OAuth adds one of your mailboxes to its own access (read and draft), or takes it out, without reconnecting and without touching other agents. Sending without approval is still granted only by a person, in the dashboard. Every change is in the audit log.
create_mailbox takes grant_to_this_app to give the app access to the new mailbox right away.

create_mailbox is safe to repeat: the same address, owner and kind return the existing mailbox (reconciled) and list it for receiving, never a copy. The answer separates registered, receiving and sending.
Receiving follows the primary MX: another provider's MX at a higher preference is a backup and no longer blocks Correio; the DNS screen explains it without asking for a change.

list_mailboxes shows the state (active, suspended or being deleted) and explains the legacy status field. The Correio tools are the same in the npm package and the hosted MCP, with the version in mailbox_list_accounts.

releases.title: Attachments in the Mail MCP
releases.summary: Agents read, download, attach and forward files over MCP, with the mailbox's own permissions and limits.

items: mailbox_get_attachment: downloads an attachment by the message id and revision, with name, size and SHA-256 hash. The local package saves it to a folder you choose; the hosted MCP returns files up to 512 KiB.
mailbox_save_draft takes new attachments and picks which to keep when editing a draft or forwarding a message (up to 10 files, 256 KiB each).
The local package reads files only from the folder you set (MEPMAIL_MAIL_UPLOAD_DIR), never from a path an email suggests.
When editing a draft or forwarding, attachments stay by default; none disappears unless the agent asks.
Editing an existing draft over MCP was refused.

releases.title: Edit your agents' access; MCP walks the whole mailbox
releases.summary: Change an agent's mailboxes, default mailbox, permissions and expiry without replacing its credential. Over MCP, the agent reads a mailbox page by page to the end and searches by sender, subject, period and unread.

items: Mail → Settings → Agents → Edit: name, mailboxes, default mailbox, Drafts, Send without approval and expiry. The agent keeps the same token; a removed mailbox loses access at once.
MCP and agent API: paged listing with a cursor (nextCursor and hasMore) to the end of the mailbox, and search by words, sender, subject, period and unread, filtered on the server before the page.
Two edits at the same time never overwrite each other: whoever saves last is asked to review.
A send the agent already queued does not go out once the mailbox or the send permission is taken away.
Agent listings with more than 50 messages per page returned an error.

releases.title: Automatic rules in Mail
releases.summary: Choose where mail from a sender or a domain goes: a folder, the Archive or another mailbox of yours, already read if you like. Handy for keeping notices, reports and newsletters out of the Inbox.

items: Create rule, next to the sender in the open message: for this sender or for any address at the domain (subdomains included).
Destinations: a folder of the mailbox, the Archive or another mailbox of yours, with mark as read and star. Optionally it also applies to messages already in the Inbox.
Preferences → Appearance → Automatic rules lists each mailbox's rules, to edit or delete.
Spam, quarantine and blocked senders are never moved by a rule. Another mailbox receives only while it is yours.
Each rule's sender or domain is encrypted, like message content.

releases.title: An agents panel in Mail, and offline reading in the app
releases.summary: The Agents tab brings together what awaits your approval, who has access and what each agent did. The MepMail desktop app can keep a copy to read without internet.

items: Agents → Awaiting approval: drafts your agents prepared, with To, Cc and Bcc, to approve or discard. The pending count shows in the sidebar.
Agents with access: scopes, mailboxes and last use of each key, with a confirmed revoke; plus each agent's recent activity.
In the desktop app, Preferences → Offline reading keeps a copy of recent messages on this computer. Signing out erases that copy.
Messages sent by an agent show "Written by agent X · approved by you".
The link in the approval email opens the draft directly.
The recipient limit counts To, Cc and Bcc, and the copy now says so.

releases.title: The Portuguese site is findable on Google
releases.summary: The public pages in Portuguese now have their own address (?lang=pt-BR), so Google can index them and show MepMail in Portuguese to people searching from Brazil.

items: Search engines send neither a cookie nor a browser language, so they only ever saw the English site. Every public page now also exists in Portuguese at ?lang=pt-BR, with its own canonical.
Every public page declares both versions (hreflang en, pt-BR and x-default), and the sitemap lists each page in both languages.
The PT/EN switch still remembers your choice; on an address with ?lang= it changes the address too.

releases.title: Delete a mailbox, with 30 days to change your mind
releases.summary: Team owners and admins can now delete a mailbox by typing its address. It stops receiving and sending at once and frees its seat in the plan; for 30 days it can be restored, and after that its mail is erased and the address is free again.

items: Manage mailbox → Delete mailbox: type the address to confirm. The mailbox is suspended right away, leaves SES receiving, and stops counting as a seat.

Restore within 30 days, as long as the plan has a free seat. After that, a worker erases its messages, folders and send records, then the mailbox itself, freeing the address and its aliases. System backups expire within 4 weeks after that.
The team audit log records each deletion and restore.

releases.title: When AWS pauses one customer, MepMail holds that customer
releases.summary: Every customer sends through its own SES tenant. When SES pauses a tenant for its reputation, MepMail now notices within 15 minutes and holds that team for review, so its mail waits instead of failing one message at a time, while every other customer keeps sending.

items: A 15-minute check reads each team's SES tenant status. A tenant SES paused puts the team on hold for review (reason: reputation): accepted mail parks, the operator is told, and an operator releases it once the cause is fixed.

releases.title: Recipes: four integrations, run end to end
releases.summary: The docs gain four recipes, each with its product, credential, events, errors and the responses we got running it in production: a support agent with human approval, triage without send, one agent over several mailboxes, and SaaS notifications.

items: docs.mepmail.dev/recipes: a support agent that drafts replies and waits for the owner's approval, read-only triage, an mmt_ key over several mailboxes with the MepMail-Mailbox header, and password-reset notifications through the Send API with an idempotency key.
The Mail API docs describe its pagination (limit up to 100 and nextCursor) and team keys, and the migration order: create every mailbox and alias, switch MX, then turn receiving on.
The integrations docs list the cloud SMTP relay (smtp.mepmail.dev, port 2587, username mepmail, a Send key as the password) and say which credential each integration uses.
The agent skill describes Mail's own plans and the mmt_ keys.

releases.title: Lists, usage and holds say what really happens
releases.summary: Lists say how many items they show out of how many, usage is labeled as counted sends, a parked email is no longer charged twice, and the broadcast pause notice no longer names internal rates.

items: An email to several recipients that was parked (SES out of sends, a pause or a review) handed back one unit and was charged again for every recipient on release. It now hands back as many as it is charged again.
Lists read “Showing 40 of 388 emails” (or “3 domains”) with correct singular and plural, instead of “Page 1 – 1 of 388 emails”, and the size chooser reads “40 at a time”.
Usage shows “sends counted” and explains that each recipient (To, Cc and Bcc) of an accepted email counts, even if delivery fails later.
The daily limit banner says a short margin still goes out and the rest waits in the queue for the next day.
The broadcast pause email and API message say broadcasts are paused to protect delivery, without naming internal rates, and the email no longer implies a manual pause is automatic.
The email asking you to approve an agent's draft now links to that draft's mailbox and message.

releases.title: MepMail explained as one product: Mail, Send and agents
releases.summary: The site now presents Mail, agent mailboxes and Send as parts of one account, says which credential each integration uses, shows the Mail trial's card and charge where you decide, and prices common setups.

items: Home: “Where to start”, with three ways in (my professional email, email for my agent, my app's emails), each with its product, price and next step.
Pricing: what common setups cost, as sums of the separate plans (no bundle), plus answers on how usage is counted and on using Mail and Send together.
Integrations: a “which credential to use” section, and each card now lists its product, endpoint, credential and permissions.
Every “7 days free” for Mail now says the trial takes a card and bills when it ends unless you cancel, and pricing lists the trial's sending limits.
Usage is described the way it is counted: each recipient (To, Cc and Bcc) counts. Mail counts outbound recipients.
The footer, the default page description, the sign-up panel and the navigation now cover Mail and Send, and the OAuth consent says which sends need your approval.
The changelog opens the latest 10 releases and folds the earlier ones, instead of promising six.
Removed the claim that one API key covers every integration: Send keys, mailbox keys and OAuth reach different things.
Removed internal wording about the operator's license from public pages, and Mail actions in the team audit log now show readable labels.

releases.title: Translate a message without it leaving your computer
releases.summary: A Translate button in the MepMail Mail reader turns a message into your language with the translator built into your browser: no server, no cost, and the text never leaves your computer.

items: Translate in the reader: the whole message in your language, with “Show original” to switch back. The first use may download the language model, with progress on screen.
It only appears where the browser has its own translator (recent Chrome on the computer), and it says so when a message is already in your language.

releases.title: MepMail Mail opens with your inbox already there
releases.summary: The mail page now arrives with your mailboxes, preferences, unread counts and the first page of the Inbox, so the inbox shows up without waiting for another round trip.

items: The server reads what MepMail Mail shows first while it renders the page. If any of it takes longer than a moment, the page goes out without it and your browser asks for it as before.
The import status is checked every 5 minutes while no import is running, and every 30 seconds during one. Starting or resuming an import refreshes it at once.

releases.title: Download the desktop app from anywhere on the site
releases.summary: A new /download page gathers the Windows and Linux apps, and the header, the footer and the home page now link to it.

items: /download: the Windows app (Microsoft Store, or the self-updating installer) and the Linux packages, with your system first, what the app adds to the browser, and the browser for Mac and phones.
An “App” link in the site header and “Windows and Linux apps” in the footer.
The home announcement about the Windows and Linux app now opens the downloads, and the MepMail Mail section links to them.

releases.title: Correio search looks through all your mail
releases.summary: Searching in Correio now asks the server, so it finds every matching message in the mailbox, or in all mailboxes, instead of only the ones already on screen.

items: The full Correio search was refused by the server and fell back to the messages already loaded. It now searches the whole mailbox, and “Search all mailboxes” searches every one of them.

releases.title: Search every mailbox, write in a corner, read mail leaves Unread
releases.summary: Correio searches all your mailboxes at once, the composer sits in a corner you can minimize, opened mail stops counting as unread right away, and the agents screen tells mailbox keys apart from team and app credentials.

items: Search across all your mailboxes, also from Ctrl+K.
The composer opens in a corner instead of a full-screen window, can be minimized while you read, and asks before it discards a draft.
In the desktop app, “Connect on this computer” sets up Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code or Codex with a new agent key, and the key shows “Connected” on its own once the agent uses it.
Opening a message marks it as read at once by default, so it leaves the Unread filter as you go. You can still choose a delay, or manual, in the Correio settings.
The agent keys of a mailbox now mark team credentials and OAuth apps. Revoking one of those revokes the whole credential, on every mailbox, and the confirmation says so.
Creating a key on a mailbox that already has 25 active keys says so, instead of a generic error.
The mail screen loads faster: the text editor downloads separately, after the page, and the inbox list is requested together with the mailbox list.
Revoking from a single mailbox no longer leaves a team credential or an OAuth app half revoked.

releases.title: The domain page says how to fix SPF
releases.summary: When the SPF row of a domain does not match, the page now says what to change instead of only showing what DNS answers.

items: An SPF record that exists without Amazon SES asks you to add include:amazonses.com to it, rather than create a second record.
Two SPF records on the same name ask you to merge them into one, since receivers treat two as broken.

releases.title: Domains verify with your own SPF includes
releases.summary: A sending domain whose SPF record already lists other senders now verifies as soon as it also includes Amazon SES, instead of waiting on an exact match.

items: The SPF check reads the record as a policy: v=spf1 with include:amazonses.com verifies even next to your own includes (for example a newsletter tool), with ~all, -all or ?all.
Two SPF records on the same name, or a record that allows everyone (+all), still read as wrong, because receivers reject them.

releases.title: Version and help in the folder rail
releases.summary: The folder rail now shows which MepMail version you are on, and opens a Help menu with what's new, keyboard shortcuts, the help center and support.

items: The rail footer shows the version (v0.119 here) instead of a question mark; the collapsed rail keeps the question mark.
Its Help menu: the version and date, the desktop app's version when you use it, What's new, Keyboard shortcuts, Help center and Talk to support.

releases.title: Unread that keeps up with you
releases.summary: With Unread on, a message leaves the list as soon as you move on from it, the counts drop at once, and one click marks the whole view as read.

items: Mark as read in the list header: every unread message in the view (pile, filter and search applied) in one step, with Undo.
With Unread on, a message you read leaves the list when you open the next one or go back; J and K and the next-after-leaving step land on the next unread message.
Unread counts in the folder rail and the tab title drop the moment a message is read.
Marking many messages read or unread is one request for up to 200 messages instead of one per message.
Marking a message unread, or undoing Mark as read, no longer shows a new-mail notice.

releases.title: Desktop app 1.0.2: MepMail as your email app
releases.summary: The desktop app can be your default email app on Windows and Linux, so mailto: links open MepMail's composer, and the tray menu gains Reload. Folders reopened within the hour skip re-fetching their keys.

items: Desktop 1.0.2 for Windows and Linux: MepMail registers as an email app for mailto: links (choose it in Default apps), opening the composer with the recipients, subject and body filled in.
Reload in the desktop tray menu.
Installed apps update themselves to 1.0.2; the Windows installer and the Linux AppImage, .deb and .rpm are on the download page.
Message keys a folder already opened stay in the server's memory for up to an hour instead of ten minutes, so reopening it skips the key service.

releases.title: Folders open with one access check
releases.summary: Listing a folder across your mailboxes, and counting unread mail, now checks access to all of them at once instead of mailbox by mailbox.

items: Inbox, Sent, Drafts and the other views list every mailbox in one database read after one access check, instead of one per mailbox.
Unread counts for the folder rail come from one grouped count.

releases.title: Fewer key lookups when opening Mail
releases.summary: When a folder opens and many messages were sealed with the same key, Mail now asks the key service once instead of once per message.

items: Opening a folder after a pause makes one key-service request per message key, shared by every message that uses it, instead of one per message.
Server timing of key lookups (from cache, from the key service, or shared) in the operator's timing log, to tune the next speed work.

releases.title: Formatted mail, Bcc and mailto links
releases.summary: Write with bold, italics, lists, links and quotes, add blind copies, and open mailto: links straight in Mail's composer. The folder rail counts load faster.

items: The composer formats text: bold, italics, bulleted and numbered lists, quotes and links. A formatted draft reopens as you left it, and every message still carries a plain-text part.
Bcc next to Cc. Blind copies receive the message and no other recipient sees them; To, Cc and Bcc share the 20-recipient limit.
mailto: links open the composer with the recipients, subject and body filled in, from a message or from the browser once MepMail is set as the handler in Appearance.
Agents can add bcc to mailbox_save_draft (hosted MCP) and to the drafts API.
Unread, Snoozed, Scheduled and Follow-up counts and the folder list load several mailboxes at once instead of one after another.
With live updates connected, Mail checks for changes less often in the background.

releases.title: Search all of Mail
releases.summary: Search now looks through every folder at once, in the subject, sender, recipients, body and attachment names, with operators and exact phrases. Mail stays sealed: the index holds keyed tokens, never text.

items: Search in Mail covers every folder at once (Trash and Spam aside) and each result shows its folder; words in the subject, sender and recipients also match by their start.
Operators: from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment, before: and after: (a day), and "exact phrase"; in Portuguese, de:, para:, assunto:, tem:anexo, antes: and depois:.
An Appearance setting to open the next message after archiving or deleting, or to go back to the list.

releases.title: Faster Mail: delete and move on without waiting
releases.summary: Deleting, archiving and marking spam no longer wait for the server before the next message, the next message opens by itself, bulk actions run in parallel and new-mail alerts arrive sooner.

items: Correio receiving on Cloudflare: in the new mailbox setup, a DNS-only token creates the domain's MX record. Where the domain already receives mail at another service, its MX is never changed.
Delete, archive and spam act on each message on its own: the next one can be removed while the server is still answering the first.
After deleting or archiving the open message, the next one in the list opens (the previous one when it was the last).
Bulk delete, move, archive and undo send their requests in parallel; a failure on some messages no longer stops the rest.
A new-message alert fetches that message along with the counters, and anything that arrived while the live connection was renewing is read as soon as it reconnects.
An open draft shows its send status once, not twice.

releases.title: MepMail app for Linux
releases.summary: The Mail desktop app now runs on Linux too: .deb, .rpm and AppImage, with tray, unread counter and automatic updates.

items: MepMail app for Linux: .deb, .rpm and AppImage, with tray, unread counter and automatic updates. Download it at mepmail.dev/desktop/correio/linux.
The home and the Mail page now start with email on your own domain, for you and your agents in the same mailbox, without hosting.

Mail: a draft that is already being sent can no longer be saved as a new version from another tab or by an agent, so it cannot turn into a second email. A refused send can still be corrected and sent.

releases.title: Plan limit emails, and Delete forever in Mail
releases.summary: Team owners on a Mail plan now get an email at 80% and at 100% of each limit and when receiving pauses, and the trash can be emptied to free storage.

items: An email at 80% and another at 100% of each plan limit (recipients and mail sent, messages and mail received, storage), once per billing month, with the renewal date and the next plan.
An email when receiving pauses, with the reason and when it starts again by itself; mail received before the pause is kept.

Empty trash, Delete forever on a message and on a selection in the trash: it frees storage at once, and a paused receiving starts again within a minute once storage fits. Sent messages stay; copies in backups go within 30 days.

releases.title: Open pages tell you when a new version is out
releases.summary: Correio and the dashboard now notice a new MepMail release while they stay open, also in the Windows app kept in the tray, and offer to reload.

items: A notice, A new version of MepMail is available, with Reload, appears when the page was opened before a release; nothing reloads by itself, so a draft is never lost.

releases.title: Get the Windows app on the Microsoft Store
releases.summary: Correio and the account menu now point to the MepMail app on the Microsoft Store, signed by Microsoft and updated by the Store; the direct installer stays as the alternative.

items: The account menu, Preferences and the Correio page open the MepMail app on the Microsoft Store; the direct installer is still offered, and apps installed from it keep updating themselves.

releases.title: The Windows app is now called MepMail
releases.summary: The Windows app 1.0.1 shows the name MepMail in its window, tray, notices, shortcuts and installed apps list, and updates itself from 1.0.0 without a second install.

items: Windows app 1.0.1: the window, tray, permission dialogs, update notices, Start menu and desktop shortcuts and Settings > Apps say MepMail; the install folder and updates stay the same.
The direct download is now MepMail_1.0.1_x64-setup.exe; the app is also on the Microsoft Store.
Correio: a purchase you started and did not pay can be left with Choose another plan, without any charge; a payment Stripe already took is kept.

releases.title: Correio plans: Solo, Duo and Equipe
releases.summary: Correio now comes in three monthly plans, with or without Send: Solo with 1 mailbox for US$ 2.90, Duo with 3 for US$ 5.90 and Equipe with 10 for US$ 12.90, shared limits, 7 days free and no overage.

items: Three plans with team-wide monthly limits: storage, recipients sent and messages received, shared by the team's mailboxes. In Brazil R$ 14.90, R$ 29.90 and R$ 64.90.
Change plan from Correio: an upgrade applies at once and charges the difference; a smaller plan applies when your usage fits, without a refund for the month.
Usage meters for every limit in Correio, with the renewal date and an upgrade button, and a notice when receiving pauses.
Past the received limit plus a 10% margin, or with storage full, receiving pauses until the next month or an upgrade; stored mail stays readable.
Contracts bought before the plans keep their price and terms, and can move to a plan when you choose.

releases.title: Correio addresses send through Correio
releases.summary: On the free Send plan, a Correio mailbox or alias address now sends from Correio, where its plan counts the recipients; the API, SMTP and broadcasts explain why and keep every other address of the domain working.

items: Sending from a Correio mailbox or alias address through the API, SMTP or a broadcast needs a paid Send plan; other addresses of the same verified domain keep the free Send plan.
Correio free trials share one daily sending ceiling on top of each trial's own 50 a day and 200 in total.
A plan change that adds mailboxes is applied only after its invoice is paid, also when the change arrives from Stripe before the confirmation.

releases.title: Choose who reaches People in Correio
releases.summary: Manage approved and blocked senders in Preferences, and move a sender the smart inbox filed under Notifications or Newsletters back to People with one click.

items: Preferences, Approved and blocked senders: per mailbox, newest first; switch between approve and block or forget a sender, with Undo; add an address before its first message; filters, search and pages once the list grows.
In the reader, a message filed under Notifications or Newsletters offers Move to People, which approves the sender (with Undo).
An approved sender counts as People in the smart inbox: in the list, the counters and the new mail notices.

releases.title: n8n reads and answers Correio
releases.summary: The n8n node 0.2.0 starts workflows when mail reaches an agent mailbox and can read messages, save reply drafts and send them, with the owner's approval when the key has no send permission.

items: n8n-nodes-mepmail 0.2.0: Mailbox Received trigger with Fetch Correio Message, a MepMail Correio API credential (mailbox key) and the Correio Message resource (Get, Get Many, Create Draft, Send Draft).
The integrations page and the docs (packages, integrations) describe the Correio flow.

releases.title: Resize Correio's columns
releases.summary: Drag the dividers between mailboxes and folders, the message list and the reader to give each column the width you want; Correio remembers it on this device.

items: Two dividers between the folder rail, the list and the reader: drag them, or use the keyboard (Tab, arrows, Shift for bigger steps, Home and End), with sensible minimum and maximum widths.
Double-click a divider to restore its default width, or use Restore default widths in the view menu; widths are saved per device and applied before the page paints.
In a narrow list the Select all bar wraps instead of overflowing, and the reader's actions stay aligned to the right when they wrap.

releases.title: A dedicated support inbox: suporte@mepmail.dev
releases.summary: Support questions now go to suporte@mepmail.dev. Leo, MepMail's support agent, prepares each reply and Jean reviews it before it is sent.

items: The support page, the chat fallback, the home, pricing and integrations pages and the agent guide (auth.md) point to suporte@mepmail.dev.
Billing, refunds, privacy and security reports still go straight to jean@mepmail.dev, as the terms and the security page say.

releases.title: A webhook when mail reaches an agent mailbox
releases.summary: Agents no longer need to poll Correio: subscribe a webhook to the new mailbox.received event and MepMail calls it as soon as a message lands in an agent mailbox's inbox.

items: mailbox.received webhook event, in a new Correio group of the event picker: it carries the mailbox and message IDs, the size and the time, never the sender, subject or body, which the agent reads with its own mailbox key or the Correio MCP.
Opt-in, like email.prefetched: endpoints receive it only when they pick it, never through All events. Person mailboxes, Spam, quarantine and history imports never fire it.

releases.title: New mail shows up the moment it arrives
releases.summary: Correio no longer waits for its next check: a new message appears in the open list and in the unread count as soon as it is received, with a notice while you are writing.

items: Live updates: a message received now refreshes the unread count and the top of the open folder at once, in the browser and in the Windows app.

A notice for new mail in any folder: inside the app, a toast with the sender and subject and an Open button, plus a line above the composer while you write; outside it, a desktop notification (or the browser's, once you allow it).
History imports stay quiet: messages brought in from another account never trigger notices.
The backup check for new mail runs every 15 seconds instead of 30 when the live connection is unavailable.

releases.title: Bring your old email into Correio
releases.summary: The migration assistant now imports an IMAP account's history (Gmail, Outlook, Purelymail, Titan and others) into a Correio mailbox, keeping folders, dates and read state.

items: History import over IMAP: pick the folders and where each one goes (Inbox, Sent, Archive or a folder of your own); dates and read state are kept, and the old account is only read.
Your password is used only while the import runs and is never saved. If the connection drops, the import resumes where it stopped once you type it again.
Bring only the history: an account whose mailboxes already exist goes straight to the import.
New-mail notices stay quiet while an import is running.

releases.title: Large emails and attachments now arrive
releases.summary: Correio receives and opens messages up to 25 MB with up to 100 attachments. Before, an email over 1 MB, or with an attachment over 256 KB, never reached the mailbox.

items: Received emails up to 25 MB, with attachments up to 25 MB, arrive, open and download in full.
Very long HTML emails are cut at 5 MB and keep their layout, instead of falling back to plain text.
Forwarding an email whose attachment is over the 256 KB sending limit says so when saving, instead of failing at send time.

releases.title: Mail with 3 mailboxes for US$ 12.90, 7 days free
releases.summary: Mail on its own now includes 3 mailboxes that share 10 GiB and 2,000 outbound deliveries, extra mailboxes cost US$ 3.90, and a first subscription starts with 7 days free. In Brazil it is charged in reais.

items: Mail without a Send plan: US$ 12.90 a month (US$ 129 a year) with 3 mailboxes, for people or agents, sharing 10 GiB and 2,000 outbound deliveries a month; each extra mailbox is US$ 3.90 a month.
In Brazil, Checkout charges in reais: R$ 64.90 a month and R$ 19.90 per extra mailbox.
7-day free trial on a first subscription, card collected up front: up to 50 recipients a day and 200 in total until the first payment, and a reminder 2 days before it ends.
The API reference names every endpoint, with summaries, a sending example and the rate-limit answer, and the docs list the n8n community node.
Lighter pages: the browser no longer downloads copy only the server uses, and the share image is ten times smaller.

releases.title: Sender approval and calendar invites
releases.summary: Correio asks before a new person reaches your Inbox, and shows calendar invitations as a card you can join or save to your calendar.

items: Sender approval: the first email from someone new shows New sender with Approve and Block. Blocking files this and future messages in Spam, with Undo; turn it off in Preferences.
Calendar invites: the invitation shows its title, the time in your time zone, place, organizer and guests, with Join meeting, Add to Google Calendar and Download invite (.ics).

releases.title: Undo send, quick replies and a smart inbox
releases.summary: Correio waits a few seconds before sending so you can take a message back, offers one-click replies, and sorts the Inbox into People, Notifications and Newsletters.

items: Undo send: Correio waits 10 seconds before sending (0, 5, 10, 20 or 30 in Preferences); undo from the notice, from the open draft or with the Z key.
Quick replies at the end of every received email: one click starts the reply with the text above your signature. Edit the list in Preferences.
Smart inbox tabs: People, Notifications, Newsletters and All, with unread counts. People you have replied to always stay in People. Turn it off in Preferences.
The Z key undoes archive and delete again.
On phones, the notice fits on one line and Settings no longer scrolls sideways.

releases.title: Plans and policies that match the product
releases.summary: Pricing, terms, privacy, security and the docs now describe limits, overage and where data is processed the way the product actually works.

items: Overage: on monthly Pro and Scale it comes switched on and can be turned off in Billing, up to 5× the included volume. Free and Starter never bill overage.
Daily limit on Free and Starter: sends keep going up to 50% past it, then wait in a queue for the next day.
Privacy and security pages say where data runs: the application and its database in Germany (Contabo), email delivery and payments in the United States, and our self-hosted analytics without cookies.
Docs limits page: sender domains 1 / 10 / 25 / unlimited, teams 1 / 3 / 10 / unlimited, unlimited contacts on every paid plan.
mepmail.dev now publishes DMARC, TLS reporting and CAA records, its SPF authorizes only Amazon SES, and www.mepmail.dev redirects to mepmail.dev.

releases.title: Support one click away in the dashboard
releases.summary: A “Support” button on every dashboard page opens the chat in its own window. Once identification is on, support already knows which account and organization the conversation is about.

items: Floating “Support” button on dashboard pages and in the sidebar, opening the support chat in its own window.
Verified identity in the chat: when you are signed in, support sees your name, email, organization, plan and mailbox count, with no billing data or email content.

releases.title: Correio app for Windows
releases.summary: Correio now has a Windows app with automatic updates. And Mail billing got safer: fraud protection also covers people who subscribe to Mail on its own.

items: Correio app for Windows, with automatic updates: download it at mepmail.dev/desktop/correio/windows or from “Windows app” in the account menu.
Mailboxes bought at the Send-plan discount move to the price of Mail without Send at the next renewal when the team goes without Send for more than 7 days; the owner gets an email notice first.
Stripe's fraud screening now also covers people who subscribe to Mail on its own.

releases.title: Mail without a Send plan
releases.summary: You can now subscribe to Mail on its own: US$ 12.90 per mailbox a month, with 10 GiB, 2,000 outbound deliveries and up to 3 domains, no Send plan needed.

items: Mail on its own: US$ 12.90 per mailbox a month or US$ 129 a year, with 10 GiB, 2,000 outbound deliveries a month and up to 3 domains. The billing account is created in the checkout itself.
With a paying Send plan, mailboxes still cost US$ 5.90 (1 GiB) or US$ 9.90 (10 GiB).
The pricing and Mail pages show both ways to subscribe, and the FAQ is updated, including the Mail MCP.

releases.title: Automatic DNS at Cloudflare
releases.summary: Domains on Cloudflare now set themselves up: paste a token that only touches DNS and MepMail creates the records and starts verification.

items: “Set up at Cloudflare” on the domain page and when adding a domain: a link opens token creation with the right permissions, and MepMail creates DKIM, MAIL FROM, SPF and, when missing, DMARC.
Nothing you already have is overwritten: a different SPF, DMARC or MX stays as it is and is marked for you to review.
The token is used for that setup only and is not saved; the action shows in the team audit log.
The Correio list got faster still in mailboxes with many HTML messages.

releases.title: A faster Correio
releases.summary: The Correio list loads much faster, folders you already visited open instantly, and messages start loading when you hover them.

items: The message list reads only what each row shows, batched per mailbox, instead of opening every message in full.
Going back to a folder shows its list at once and refreshes in the background; hovering a folder or a message starts loading it.
The reader shows subject, sender and date while the body arrives.
Across the dashboard, each query arrives as soon as it is ready, so one slow answer no longer holds the others.

releases.title: A quieter cookie notice
releases.summary: The advertising cookie notice is smaller: one sentence, the policy link and two equally sized choices, without covering the page.

items: Compact cookie notice in the corner, with “Decline” and “Accept” side by side at the same size; on phones it is a thin strip along the bottom.
The full preferences are still under “Advertising preferences” in the site footer.

releases.title: Snooze, pin and send later
releases.summary: Correio can now snooze messages, pin them to the top of the inbox, send later and remind you when nobody replies. With your advertising consent, a completed sign-up now counts for ads.

items: Snooze: the message leaves the inbox and comes back to the top at the time you pick, with the B key, quick suggestions or “Pick a date and time…”.
Pin to top: pinned messages sit in a “Pinned” section at the top of the inbox.
Send later, next to Send, cancellable until the scheduled time. At send time the license, plan, seat and domain are checked again.
“Remind me if no reply” on sent messages: with no reply by the date, the conversation comes back to the inbox.
Snoozed, Follow-ups and Scheduled folders in the sidebar with counts, and badges on the rows.

With advertising consent, a completed sign-up is also reported to Meta and Google, with only their own cookie identifiers and no email or name. Withdrawing consent cancels anything not yet sent, and the privacy policy describes it.
Consent given on the Correio, Resend alternative and integrations pages now covers the purchase events, as it already did on the home and pricing pages.

releases.title: Move to, with search
releases.summary: Moving messages got faster: a searchable menu that also creates the folder on the spot, in bulk and with the V key, with undo on every bulk action.

items: “Move to” with search: the mailbox's folders with their colors, “Remove from folder” and “Create folder and move” when the name does not exist yet.
The same menu in the selection bar, when the selected messages share a mailbox, and with the V key; on phones it opens as a bottom sheet.
Undo on every bulk action: folder, favorite, spam, inbox, archive and trash.
Dragging or bulk-moving to a folder also works in the all-mailboxes view.

releases.title: All your mailboxes in one sidebar
releases.summary: Mail gets a sidebar with every mailbox and its unread count, an account menu, a collapsible rail and a drawer on phones. And account emails now arrive in the language you use in the dashboard.

items: A sidebar with All mailboxes, People and Agents groups and each mailbox's unread count; mailbox actions sit in a “···” menu.
The rail collapses to icons (on its own on medium screens) and becomes a drawer on phones.
An account menu with system, light or dark theme, language, shortcuts, preferences, support and sign out.
The list refreshes only its first page every 15 seconds, and the unread count keeps updating while the window is minimized.
Account emails (welcome, reminders and notices) arrive in your dashboard language; people who signed in with Google could get them in English.

releases.title: From the first test to the first real send
releases.summary: After the test send, MepMail shows the next step, adding your domain, and reminds you by email in the first days if it is not verified yet.

items: In Getting started, a “Next step” card appears after the test send: add your domain, or finish verifying the one you added, with its deadline.
Getting-started reminders by email, each sent once: the domain is missing, finish the domain's DNS before the deadline, and an offer of help in the chat after three days.
The reminders can be turned off under Settings → Notifications → Getting started.

releases.title: A message list that is easier to read
releases.summary: The inbox groups messages by date, shows each sender's initials, loads more messages with no limit and lets you undo bulk actions.

items: Today, Yesterday and Last 7 days sections that stay at the top while you scroll.
Colored initials for each sender next to the message (you can hide them in the View menu).
“Load more” at the end of the list, without the old 50-message limit; J on the last row loads too.
A “new messages” notice when mail arrives while you are further down the list.
Undo for bulk mark read or unread, move to folder and spam; “mark as unread” in the reader.
When Mail opens, density, preview and reading pane already look the way you left them, with no flash of the defaults.

releases.title: Easy folders and an inbox your way
releases.summary: Create folders from any screen, give them a color and an order, and tune how the inbox looks: density, preview, reading pane, theme and start folder.

items: A “+ New folder” button that is always visible, including in the all-mailboxes view (you pick the mailbox), with create and rename right in the list; Shift+N creates a folder from the keyboard.
Each folder has a menu to rename it, pick one of eight colors, move it up or down and remove it; in the all-mailboxes view, folders are grouped by mailbox.
A View menu with density, preview lines, reading pane position and sender initials.
An Appearance tab in Mail settings: system, light or dark theme, start folder, mark as read after a few seconds and shortcut hints. Everything is saved to your account.

releases.title: The groundwork for the new inbox
releases.summary: The Mail server now returns the list in pages, conversations with unread counts, folders with a color and an order, and display preferences saved to your account. The new interface uses this in the next versions.

items: The message list comes in pages, with no 50-item limit, and can group each conversation into one row with its message total and how many are unread.
Folders get a color and a manual order; the ones you have keep their alphabetical order, and new ones go last.
Your display preferences (theme, density, reading pane, start folder, preview) are saved to your account and apply on every device.
The Mail agent API lists messages in pages with a cursor and a limit.
Optional Meta and Google Analytics measurement, only after you allow it, now also covers the Resend comparison and integrations pages.

releases.title: Bring your addresses from another provider
releases.summary: An assistant in Mail finds which addresses of your old account receive mail and creates the mailboxes and aliases at once, before you switch the MX.

items: In Mail → Settings → Migration, connect the old account over IMAP (Purelymail, Titan, Gmail, Outlook or another server). MepMail reads only headers to see which addresses on your domains receive mail, how much, and the latest.
Pick what becomes a mailbox, what becomes an alias of a mailbox and what stays out; the summary shows what will be created and whether licenses are missing.
Per domain, the assistant lists addresses that still have no mailbox or alias and the MX state, so the switch rejects no mail.
The password is used once to sign in and is not stored; message bodies are never read. History import comes next.

releases.title: Subscriptions measured in Google Analytics
releases.summary: When someone who allowed advertising measurement subscribes to a paid Send plan, it now counts as a purchase in Google Analytics, sent by our server.

items: The initial purchase of any paid Send plan is sent to Google Analytics as a purchase, with the plan and amount, only for people who allowed it in Advertising preferences.
Withdrawing permission cancels anything not yet sent and erases the Google Analytics identifier kept at checkout.

releases.title: Aliases for Mail inboxes
releases.summary: An inbox now receives at several addresses on its domain: support@ and contact@ can land straight in jean@, without another inbox.

items: Aliases: in Manage mailbox, add up to 20 addresses on the same domain that deliver into that mailbox. A message sent to the inbox and one of its aliases at once arrives only once.
An alias starts receiving once the domain's receiving (MX) is confirmed; on a domain that already receives, it works right away.
Optional Google Analytics measurement on public pages (home, pricing and Mail), only after you allow it in Advertising preferences. If you had allowed only Meta before, you are asked again.
In English, Correio is now called MepMail Mail across the dashboard, account emails and support.

releases.title: Correio over MCP without pasting a key
releases.summary: The main MCP server now reads and writes Correio mail over OAuth: you tick the mailboxes in the browser and the agent connects, with no key to copy.

items: New mail:read, mail:draft and mail:send permissions on the hosted MCP (https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp), with the mailbox_list_accounts, mailbox_list_messages, mailbox_read_message, mailbox_save_draft and mailbox_send_draft tools.
On the authorization screen you choose which of your mailboxes the app may use. Sending without approval starts unticked; without it, each send asks for your approval by email.
The connection shows up in Correio → Settings → Agents as a credential marked "connected over OAuth", with its last use, and is revoked in one click there or in Connected apps.
The Agents tab shows the command to connect without a key.

releases.title: Receiving (MX) assistant in Correio
releases.summary: When you create a mailbox, Correio shows where the domain's DNS lives, the exact MX record to copy and where mail goes today.

items: While the domain's MX is not pointed yet, the domain step detects the DNS host (Cloudflare, Registro.br, GoDaddy, Route 53, Hostinger, Locaweb or other) and shows its steps, with a button to open its panel.
The record to create is ready, with copy buttons for name and value; on a subdomain the name is already relative to the zone.
If the domain already receives mail elsewhere (Google, Microsoft, Purelymail, Titan and others), a warning explains that changing the MX sends all mail to Correio and suggests a subdomain.
A Check now button looks at DNS again without leaving the screen.

releases.title: Connecting agents to Correio got easier
releases.summary: A ready setup for each MCP client, a connection test, each key's health and an email before a key expires.

items: When you create an agent key, pick the client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Codex or other) and copy the command or configuration with the key already in it.
Test connection button: the dashboard calls the Correio MCP with the new key and lists the mailboxes it reaches.
Each key shows whether it is in use, when it was last used and the agent's last send.
A week before a key expires, the person who made it gets an email to swap it; shortcuts for 30 days, 90 days, 1 year or no expiry.
The MCP's OAuth issuer is now https://mepmail.dev; tokens issued before keep working until they expire.
The MCP server card uses the official registry name (io.github.JE4NVRG/mepmail) and no longer names old domains.

releases.title: New email notifications in Correio
releases.summary: With Correio open in another tab, the browser tells you when email arrives.

items: A bell button at the top of the inbox turns on browser notifications for new email; clicking one opens the message.
The conversation count sits on the sender's line.

releases.title: Conversations in Correio
releases.summary: Replies and original messages are now linked: the list shows how many messages a conversation has and the reading pane shows the earlier ones.

items: In the list, a number next to the sender shows how many messages the conversation has.
When you open a message, the others from the same conversation (received and sent) show above it; click to read each one.

releases.title: Undo and an unread filter in Correio
releases.summary: Archived or deleted by mistake? Now you can undo it. And one click shows only unread mail.

items: "Undo" shows for a few seconds after archiving or trashing one or several messages. The shortcut is Z.
An "Unread" button in the Inbox shows only the messages you have not opened.
Moving a message to the trash keeps you in the folder you were in.

releases.title: Keyboard shortcuts in Correio
releases.summary: The inbox has keyboard shortcuts and clearer copy.

items: Shortcuts: J and K move between messages, R replies, A replies all, F forwards, C composes, E archives, # moves to trash, S stars, U marks unread, / searches and Esc goes back to the list.
Press ? (or the ? button at the top) to see every shortcut.
The reading pane no longer shows "All mailboxes" when no message is open.
Empty-inbox and usage copy fits one or several mailboxes, and the storage bar is visible.

releases.title: One-click support from the dashboard
releases.summary: Signed-in users reach the support chat straight from the dashboard and from Correio.

items: A "Support" item in the dashboard sidebar opens the support page with the chat already open.
A "Support" button at the top of Correio opens it in a new tab, so your inbox stays open.

releases.title: A more useful support chat
releases.summary: The support chat assistant has a fuller knowledge base and the support page explains better what it does.

items: The assistant answers about DNS and domain verification, SMTP, API limits, creating Correio mailboxes and billing.
It makes clear Correio has no free plan and points to jean@mepmail.dev for account, billing and security.
The chat card on /support uses plainer language.

releases.title: Clearer copy on the site and in the dashboard
releases.summary: Copy and state fixes from a screen-by-screen review: what each MCP mode offers, one price format and Correio mailboxes shown as active.

items: Working Correio mailboxes show as "Active" instead of "Preparing".
The landing page says the hosted MCP has the full toolset and the local package covers the core sending tools.
The landing FAQ talks about the Free plan instead of a beta, and the pricing page copy is more direct.
Prices use one format everywhere (US$ 29), and the public menu calls the product Mail.
A broadcast refused during a protective pause shows a plain notice, without internal metrics.
The billing page shows a notice with "Try again" when it cannot load, instead of loading forever.

releases.title: One agent, several Correio mailboxes
releases.summary: One credential lets an agent work in several mailboxes: it names the mailbox per request, like "get the code in mailbox X" or "reply from mailbox Y".

items: Correio → Settings → Agents: "Connect an agent to several mailboxes" creates a credential (mmt_) for your active mailboxes, with an optional default mailbox.
On the Correio MCP every tool takes the mailbox address, and mailbox_list_accounts shows which ones are allowed.
Every mailbox keeps its own permissions, limits, send approval and activity record; a mailbox outside the credential is refused.

releases.title: Support chat on the support page
releases.summary: The /support page has a chat: the assistant answers from the published FAQ and hands over to Jean when a person is needed.

items: Support chat at mepmail.dev/support: the virtual assistant answers from MepMail's published content, in Portuguese or English.
Requests for a person, account, billing or security questions go to Jean, who carries on in the same chat.
The chat loads only when you click it and receives no data from your account.

releases.title: Support FAQ updated
releases.summary: Support page answers now reflect open Correio and the published prices.

items: The FAQ said Correio was closed and unpriced; it now explains the US$ 9.90/month per mailbox add-on on any paid Send plan.
Agents: the FAQ points to the Correio MCP for mailboxes.

releases.title: Received email closer to the original
releases.summary: Buttons, spacing and images show as the sender designed them, without giving up privacy.

items: Spacing with more than one value (like 12px 24px or 0 auto) was dropped; buttons now show at the right size.
Blocked images left empty gaps: their alt text now shows in their place.
Tracking pixels (1×1 images) are removed: they never load, even when you show images.
When you show images, background images show too, only from safe public addresses.
“Always show from …”: choose to show a domain's images automatically on this browser.

releases.title: Direct contact with the owner
releases.summary: Every page now points to jean@mepmail.dev, the MepMail owner's email.

items: Support, security, privacy, refunds and terms use jean@mepmail.dev as the contact, on MepMail's own domain.
security.txt points to that address too.

releases.title: Recipients as chips and suggested contacts
releases.summary: While writing, each address becomes a chip when you type a comma, and Correio suggests people you already use.

items: To and Cc as chips: comma, semicolon, Enter or Tab close an address; pasting a list splits it at once.
An invalid address turns red and sending asks you to fix it. Backspace brings the last chip back to edit; so does a double click.
Suggestions while you type: people you used on this browser, sent to, or heard from. No-reply senders are left out.
A “+ Cc” button next to To, easy to find.
From, To and Cc each take the full row in the composer, with room for several addresses.
Composer notices (like an address to fix) show in the footer next to the buttons, without scrolling.

releases.title: Reply all, Cc and quoting in Correio
releases.summary: Replies carry the original message quoted, you can copy more people, and phones get more room.

items: Reply all: includes everyone in To and Cc on the original, without repeating you.
A Cc field in the composer. To and Cc together allow up to 20 recipients.
A reply starts with the original message quoted below your signature.
Agents connected through the API or MCP can put recipients in Cc, and their drafts go out with the mailbox signature.
Logos and images stored in MepMail itself show at once, at the right size, without the external-images prompt.
On phones the Correio bar fits on one row, leaving more room for the list.
Reply no longer re-attaches the original message's files; only Forward carries attachments.

releases.title: Professional signatures in Correio
releases.summary: Each mailbox gets a signature with name, title, company, phone, website and logo, and email goes out formatted.

items: Signature editor in Settings → Mailboxes, with a live preview of what recipients see. A mailbox owner edits theirs; admins edit any.
Signature logo: upload PNG, JPG or WebP, and we size it for email.
Correio email goes out in two versions: formatted, with the signature, clickable links and quotes, and as text for those who don't read HTML.

releases.title: Read, archive and drag in Correio
releases.summary: The inbox gets the basics of professional email: unread mail stands out, an Archive, and dragging to folders.

items: New messages show in bold with a dot. The Inbox shows how many are unread, and so does the browser tab.
Opening a message marks it read; you can mark it unread again.
Archive folder: archive to take a message out of the Inbox without deleting it, and bring it back any time.
Drag messages to Inbox, Favorites, Archive, Spam, Trash or your folders. With several selected, they all go together.
With messages selected: archive, mark as read or unread, and move to the trash in one go.
The list keeps arrival order: starring, archiving or filing a message no longer moves it.

releases.title: A cleaner inbox
releases.summary: Correio shows more mail per screen, with readable previews and a tidy reading toolbar.

items: The list fits about twice as many emails per screen: sender and date, subject and one preview line.
Previews show the words you would read, without link and image addresses. Dates read like mail apps: the time today, “Yesterday”, the weekday, then the date.
When reading, Reply and Forward sit on the left; move to folder, favorite, spam and trash on the right. On a phone it all fits in two rows.
An open email takes the full height of the screen and scrolls once.
While subscriptions are paused, the pause notice takes the announcement's place at the top of the site, and the header badge no longer covers the menu.

releases.title: Clear rules against scams
releases.summary: The Terms of Service and the Refund Policy now spell out what happens to accounts used for scams.

items: The Terms explicitly forbid impersonating people, brands or institutions, using domains you do not control, and switching sender or account to escape blocks.
Signs of phishing or fraud lead to an immediate suspension, even before the first send: keys are revoked, domains leave sending and the queue is canceled.
Accounts suspended for abuse get no refund, not even within the 7-day guarantee.

releases.title: New sign-in and sign-up screens
releases.summary: Each access screen now says what it is for, in your language.

items: Sign-in welcomes you back; sign-up lists what you get: 100 emails a day free with no credit card, a Resend-compatible API, SMTP and MCP, and Correio inboxes for you and your agents.
The personalization illustration is drawn in the page's language instead of an English picture.
Signed in, the site header no longer overlaps its menu.

releases.title: Phone polish and legal pages fixed
releases.summary: The Terms, Privacy and Refund pages read correctly again, and the site is easier to use on a phone.

items: Accents in the Terms, Privacy and Refund pages display correctly again.
Template previews on the home page show sample text instead of raw merge fields.
The ad-measurement notice takes about a third of a phone screen instead of half, with both choices side by side.
Larger tap targets for footer links and the sign-up updates box, and more readable badges.

releases.title: Queued-sending notice
releases.summary: When the email provider pauses delivery, the dashboard says so and your mail waits in the queue.

items: A notice on every dashboard page while delivery is paused upstream: mail is still accepted and goes out on its own once delivery resumes.
Account, password and notice emails from MepMail itself keep flowing through a backup relay while delivery is paused.

releases.title: Sending protection for new accounts
releases.summary: New accounts start with a review step before they can send at volume, so one abusive sender cannot put everyone's deliverability at risk.

items: A new account sends a limited volume per day during its first days; our team reviews it once and the limit lifts. Mail past it is kept and sent after the review, never dropped.

Sending is held for review when a new account looks like phishing: imitated banks, insurers, carriers or security notices (now in French and Spanish too), sender addresses that keep changing, or a sending domain on a TLD known for abuse.
An account whose bounces or complaints cross the provider's review lines has all of its mail held, transactional included, until we review it.
When the email provider pauses sending, accepted mail waits in the queue and goes out once sending resumes, instead of failing.

releases.title: MCP on api.mepmail.dev
releases.summary: The official MCP now lives at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp. Agents already connected on the old address keep working.

items: Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp, with the same OAuth sign-in on mepmail.dev.
The old api-mepmail.je4ndev.com/mcp address stays up and tokens from one work on the other: nobody has to reconnect.

releases.title: MepMail now lives on mepmail.dev
releases.summary: The API, the docs and SMTP have mepmail.dev addresses. The old ones keep working, nothing to change in your code.

items: API at https://api.mepmail.dev, docs at https://docs.mepmail.dev and SMTP at smtp.mepmail.dev (port 2587, STARTTLS).
The Mail MCP also answers at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp/correio.
The dashboard, the site, the docs and the code samples now show the new addresses.
The je4ndev.com addresses stay up for existing integrations; the old docs redirect to the new ones. The main OAuth MCP stays at api-mepmail.je4ndev.com/mcp for now.

close.title: See the next release as it lands.
close.body: Create a free account and follow the product from the inside — the beta is open, no card required.
